Extent: Written testimonies by Hungarian Roma Holocaust Survivors.

Keywords: social situation, culture, poverty, Roma Holocaust, life path, Roma.

Since May 1940 2,500 Sinti and Roma from Germany were put into camps and ghettos in the General Government. Sinti and Roma on Polish territory were deported to concentration and extermination camps like Auschwitz-Birkenau, Treblinka or Majdanek. It is estimated that 35,000 Roma were killed during the war.

After 1943, the racial legislation was repealed. Overall, some 600 Libyan Jews died in the Holocaust.

For this country there are no sufficient findings on the history of Roma during the Second World War. EHRI would be pleased to receive any information

Around 6,500 Roma were racially categorised by official authorities, many were deported into the detention camps Lety near Pisek and Hodonin near Kunstadt and later deported to Auschwitz. The Roma population in Bohemia and Moravia was almost completely destroyed. 

The policy towards Roma was based on racial laws and aimed at their genocidal extermination. From May 1942, Roma from the whole country were systematically deported to camps within the country, especially to the Jasenovac camp, where they were tortured and killed. Roma were also deported to camps in Nazi Germany (Auschwitz, Dachau)

 At least 134 Roma were killed at the Paneriai mass extermination site near Vilnius in 1942 and in the spring of 1944. Many Roma were imprisoned in forced labour camps such as Pabradė, Ežerėlis, and Raudonplynė, and later hundreds were deported to Germany and occupied territories. Overall, at least 500 Lithuanian Roma were murdered during the Nazi occupation.
